XXII.|OF THE APOSTLES.|357}}</noinclude>of the law of the fathers, an emulátour of the Law as also al you are this day: {{verse|chapter=22|verse=4}}† who {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 8, 3.''}}* persecuted this vvay vnto death, binding & deliuering into custodies men & women, {{verse|chapter=22|verse=5}}† as the high Priest doth giue me testimonie, and al the auncients. of vvhom {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 9, 2.''}}* receiuing letters also to the brethren, I vvent to Damascus, that I might bring them thence bound to Hierusalem, to be punished. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=6}}† And it came to passe as I vvas going, and drawing nigh to Damascus at midday, sodenly from heauen there shone round about me much light: {{verse|chapter=22|verse=7}}† and falling on the ground, I heard a voice saying to me, Saul, Saul, vvhy persecutest thou me? {{verse|chapter=22|verse=8}}† And I answered, Vvho art thou Lord? And he said to me, I am {{sc|Iesvs}} of Nazareth, vvhom thou persecutest. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=9}}† And they that vvere vvith me, savv the light in deede, but the voice they heard not of him that spake with me. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=10}}† And I said, Vvhat shal I doe Lord? And our Lord said to me, Arise and goe to Damascus: and there it shal be told thee of al things that thou must doe. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=11}}† And vvhereas I did not see for the brightnesse of that light, being led of my companions by the hand, I came to Damascus. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=12}}† And one Ananias, a man according to the Law hauing testimonie of al the Ievves inhabitants, {{verse|chapter=22|verse=13}}† comming to me, and standing by me, said to me, Brother Saul, looke vp. And I the self same houre looked vp on him. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=14}}† But he said, The God of our fathers hath prëordained thee, that thou shouldest knovv his wil, and see the iust one, and heare a voice from his mouth: {{verse|chapter=22|verse=15}}† because thou shalt be his witnes to al men, of those things vvhich thou hast seen and heard. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=16}}† And now what tariest thou? Rise vp, and be baptized, & {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The Sacrament of Baptisme doth it self vvash away sinnes as here is plaine, & therfore doth not only signifie (as the Heretikes affirme) that our sinnes be forgiuen before, or othervvise by faith only remitted. Vvhereby the Churches doctrine is proued to be fully agreable to the Scriptures, that the Sacraments giue grace ''ex opere operato'', that is, by the force & vertue of the vvorke and vvord, done & said in the Sacrament.}}∷ vvash avvay thy sinnes inuocating his name. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=17}}† And it befel me returning into Hierusalem, and praying in the temple, that I vvas in a traunce, {{verse|chapter=22|verse=18}}† and savv him saying vnto me, Make hast, and depart quickely out of Hierusalem: because they vvil not receiue thy testimonie of me. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=19}}† And I said, Lord, they know that I did cast into prison and beate in euery synagogue them that beleeued in thee. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=20}}† And vvhen the bloud of Steuen thy {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''μάρτυρος. Act. 7, 38.''}}∷ vvitnes vvas shed, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Act. 7, 38. · μάρτυρος. · Not only the Principals but al that consent to the death or vexation of Christian men for the Catholike faith, do highly offend. vvhich the Apostle confesseth here, that Gods mercie may be more notoriously glorified in him hereby.}}∷ I stoode by and consented, and kept the garments of them that killed him. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=21}}† And he said to me, Goe, for into the Gentiles a farre vvil I send thee.

{{verse|chapter=22|verse=22}}† And they heard him vntil this vvord, and they lifted vp their voice, saying, Avvay vvith such an one from the earth: for it is not meete he should liue. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=23}}† And when they cried<noinclude>{{rh||Yy iij|out,}}</noinclude>
